Musaddad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, Abd Allah al-Danaj narrated to us, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The sun and the moon will be wrapped up (yukawwaran) on the Day of Resurrection." [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3200.]

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, and this is his wording. He narrated it in the Book of "The Beginning of Creation." It would have been appropriate for him to mention it here or to repeat it, as is his habit in such cases! Al-Bazzar has narrated it and given a better transmission. He said:

Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Abd Allah al-Danaj, who said: I heard Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Qasri in this mosque, the Mosque of Kufah, and al-Hasan came and sat with him, and he narrated: Abu Hurayrah narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the sun and the moon are two lights in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Hasan said: "And what is their sin?" He said: "I narrate to you from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and you say: 'I suppose he said: And what is their sin?'"

Then al-Bazzar said: This is not narrated from Abu Hurayrah except through this chain, and Abd Allah al-Danaj did not narrate from Abu Salamah anything other than this hadith.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the stars fall (inkadarat)﴾, it means: they were scattered, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾ (Surah al-Infitar, 2). The original meaning of inkidar is to pour down (al-insiba).

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "There are six signs before the Day of Resurrection. While people are in their markets, the light of the sun goes away. While they are in that state, the stars are scattered. While they are in that state, the mountains fall upon the face of the earth, and they shake, tremble and become mixed up. The jinn flee to mankind and mankind flee to the jinn, and the beasts, birds and wild animals become mixed together, and they surge against one another." ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: he said: they were mixed together. ﴿And when the pregnant camels are neglected﴾: he said: their people abandon them. ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: he said: the jinn said: "We will bring you the news." He said: So they went to the sea, and behold, it was a fire blazing. He said: While they were in that state, the earth split open in one crack, down to the lowest seventh earth and up to the highest seventh heaven. He said: While they were in that state, the wind came upon them and killed them."

Ibn Jarir narrated it, and this is his wording, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated part of it. Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu Salih, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman and al-Dahhak said the same regarding ﴿And when the stars fall﴾: it means they were scattered.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾ means: they changed. Yazid ibn Abi Maryam narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding ﴿And when the stars fall﴾: he said: "They fall into Hell, and everyone who worshipped other than Allah is in Hell, except for what was of Jesus and his mother. If they had been content to be worshipped, they would have entered it." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with the previously mentioned chain.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, it means: they departed from their places and were blown away, so they left the earth level and bare.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the pregnant camels are neglected﴾: Ikrimah and Mujahid said: they are the pregnant she-camels. Mujahid said: ﴿neglected﴾ means left and let loose.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b and al-Dahhak said: their people abandoned them. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: they were not milked and their udders were not tied; their owners left them. Al-Dahhak said: they were left without a shepherd.

The meaning in all of this is close. The intended meaning is that the pregnant camels (ishar), which are the best of camels and the pregnant ones that have reached the tenth month of their pregnancy, whose singular is 'ushara', and which keep this name until they give birth, have been neglected by people, who are busy with other things, and with their care and benefit from them, although previously they had been the most desired of things to them, because of the great, terrifying and dreadful matter that overwhelms them, which is the matter of the Resurrection, the establishment of its causes, and the occurrence of its preliminaries.

It was said: Rather, this will happen on the Day of Resurrection, and its owners will see it in that state, with no way for them to reach it. It has also been said regarding the ishar that they are the clouds, which are held back from moving between heaven and earth because of the ruin of the world. It has also been said that they are the lands that are tithed (tu'ashsharu). It was said that they are the dwellings that were inhabited, which become abandoned because their people have gone. Imam Abu Abd Allah al-Qurtubi related all these opinions in his book "al-Tadhkirah," and he preferred that they are the camels, and attributed this to most people. [Footnote: Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah, pp. 212–213.]

I say: Rather, nothing is known from the earlier generations and the imams other than this. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾, it means: they are assembled, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies with its wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 38). Ibn Abbas said: every creature will be gathered, even the fly. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Suddi and others said the same. Qatadah also said regarding the explanation of this verse: these creatures will be [present], and Allah will decide concerning them what He wills.

Ikrimah said: their gathering is their death.

Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi narrated to me, Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, Husayn informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: He said: the gathering of the beasts is their death, and the gathering of everything is death, except the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym regarding ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: He said: the command of Allah came upon them. Sufyan said: my father said: I mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: their gathering is their death.

It has already been mentioned from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he said regarding ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: they became mixed together.

Ibn Jarir said: The more preferable view is that of the one who said ﴿gathered﴾ means "brought together," as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the birds gathered (mahshurah)﴾ (Surah Sad, 19), meaning: assembled.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze (sujjirat)﴾: Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to a man from the Jews: "Where is Hell?" He said: "The sea." He said: "I do not think he is except truthful." [Qur'an: ﴿And by the sea that is set ablaze (al-masjur)﴾ (Surah al-Tur, 6), ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ (sujjirat, with a lightened form).] [Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (30/43).]

Ibn Abbas and others said: Allah will send upon them the dabur wind, which will ignite them, and they will become fire blazing. The discussion of this has already been mentioned at His saying ﴿And by the sea that is set ablaze﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Tahir narrated to us, Abd al-Jabbar ibn Sulayman Abu Sulayman al-Naffat narrated to me (a righteous shaykh who resembles Malik ibn Anas), from Mu'awiyah ibn Sa'id, who said: This sea is a blessing (the Mediterranean, the Sea of the Romans) in the middle of the earth, and all the rivers pour into it, and the great sea pours into it, and at its bottom are wells sealed with copper. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will be set ablaze.

This is a strange and remarkable report. In Sunan Abi Dawud: "No one rides the sea except a pilgrim, a one performing umrah, or a warrior in the way of Allah, for beneath the sea is fire, and beneath the fire is sea," and the hadith... The discussion of it was previously mentioned in Surah Fatir. [Footnote: The discussion of the hadith did not previously occur in Surah Fatir. It is in Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2489, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with both of them.]

Mujahid and al-Hasan ibn Muslim said: ﴿sujjirat﴾ means "ignited (uqidat)." Al-Hasan said: it dried up. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: its water receded and went away, leaving not a drop in it. Al-Dahhak also said: ﴿sujjirat﴾ means "burst open (fujjirat)." Al-Suddi said: it was opened and made to flow. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: ﴿sujjirat﴾ means "overflowed."

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired (zuwwijat)﴾, it means: every kind is gathered with its counterpart, like His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 22).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "They are the peers (al-darba'), every man with every people whose deeds he used to do." That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And you will be three kinds: the companions of the right hand, what are the companions of the right hand; and the companions of the left hand, what are the companions of the left hand; and the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 7-10]. He said: They are the peers. [[Also narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/429).]]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through other chains, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that Umar addressed the people and recited ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾, and said: "Its pairing is that every group is joined to its own group." In another narration: "They are two men who do a deed by which they enter Paradise or the Fire." [[Also narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Hamdan, as cited in the author's Musnad Umar (2/620), through Khalaf ibn al-Walid, from Israel, from Simak, similarly. It was also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (2/284-285), from al-Thawri, from Simak, from al-Nu'man, and from Israel, from Simak, from al-Nu'man. And al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/515) through Sufyan, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

In another narration from al-Nu'man: Umar was asked about the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾, and he said: "A righteous man is paired with a righteous man, and an evil man is paired with an evil man in the Fire; that is the pairing of souls."

In another narration from al-Nu'man: Umar said to the people: "What do you say about the interpretation of this verse: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾?" They were silent. He said: "Rather, it is that a man is paired with his counterpart from the people of Paradise, and a man is paired with his counterpart from the people of the Fire." Then he recited: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "That is when people are in three kinds."

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "The likes among people are gathered together." Similarly said al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Hasan, and Qatadah. Ibn Jarir chose this view, and it is the correct one.

Another opinion regarding His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ash'ath [ibn Sawwar] [[Addition from M.]], from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "A valley flows from the base of the Throne with water between the two blasts, and the time between them is forty years. From it every creature that has decayed grows, whether human, bird, or beast. If a passer-by had known them before that, he would recognize them on the earth, having sprouted. Then the spirits are sent, and the bodies are paired with them." That is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾.

Similarly said Abu al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, and also al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: meaning, they are paired with bodies. It was also said: The believers are paired with the wide-eyed houris, and the disbelievers are paired with devils. This was related by al-Qurtubi in al-Tadhkirah. [[Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah (p. 213).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾. This is the reading of the majority: ﴿su'ilat﴾ [was asked]. The one buried alive (al-maw'udah) is the girl whom the people of the Jahiliyyah used to bury in the dust out of aversion to daughters. On the Day of Resurrection, the buried girl will be asked for what sin she was killed, so that this would be a threat to her killer. If the wronged one is asked, then what is the assumption about the wrongdoer?!

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked﴾, meaning: she demanded. Similarly said Abu al-Duha: "She demanded," meaning: she sought retribution for her blood. And from al-Suddi and Qatadah, the same. [[See Tafsir al-Tabari (30/45) and al-Bahr al-Muhit of Abu Hayyan (8/433).]]

Traditions have been related concerning the buried girl. Imam Ahmad said:
Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Abu al-Aswad, namely Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal, narrated to me, from Urwah, from Aishah, from Judamah bint Wahb, the sister of Ukkashah, who said: I attended the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among some people, and he was saying: "I had intended to forbid ghilah (secret intercourse during breastfeeding), but I looked at the Romans and the Persians, and they practice ghilah with their children, and that does not harm their children at all." Then they asked him about 'azl (coitus interruptus), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is the hidden burial (al-wad' al-khafi), and it is the one of whom it is said: ﴿the buried girl will be asked﴾."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri', namely Abd Allah ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub. [[Al-Musnad (6/434) and Sahih Muslim, no. 1442.]] Ibn Majah also narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yahya ibn Ishaq al-Sayhalini, from Yahya ibn Ayyub. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2011.]] Muslim also narrated it, as did Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Malik ibn Anas; all three from Abu al-Aswad, with the same chain. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1442; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3882; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2077; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/106).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Alqamah, from Salamah ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, who said: My brother and I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, our mother Mulaykah used to keep the ties of kinship, host guests, and do [and do] [[Addition from M or al-Musnad.]], and she died in the Jahiliyyah. Will that benefit her at all?" He said: "No." We said: "She used to bury our sister alive in the Jahiliyyah. Will that benefit her at all?" He said: "The one who buries and the one who is buried are in the Fire, unless Islam reaches the one who buries, and Allah pardons her."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (3/478) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11649.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Alqamah and Abu al-Ahwas, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one who buries and the one who is buried are in the Fire." [[Also narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4717, through Abu Ishaq, from Amir, from Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud. It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/114), through Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi, from Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud.]]

Ahmad also said: Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, Awf informed us, Hasna' bint Mu'awiyah al-Suraymiyyah narrated to me, from her paternal uncle, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is in Paradise?" He said: "The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyr is in Paradise, the newborn is in Paradise, and the buried girl is in Paradise." [[Al-Musnad (5/58).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Qurrah narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is in Paradise?" He said: "The buried girl is in Paradise."

This is a mursal hadith from the mursal narrations of al-Hasan, and some have accepted it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Zahrani narrated to me, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The children of the polytheists are in Paradise. Whoever claims that they are in the Fire has lied. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾." Ibn Abbas said: "She is the one buried."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel informed us, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked [for what sin she was killed]﴾ [[Addition from A.]], who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I buried daughters of mine alive in the Jahiliyyah." He said: "Free a slave for each one of them." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a man with camels?" He said: "Then sacrifice a camel for each one of them."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar, the hafiz, said: Abd al-Razzaq was contradicted in this, and we did not write it except from al-Husayn ibn Mahdi, from him. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2280 (Kashf al-Astar).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, saying: Abu Abd Allah al-Zahrani informed us, in what he wrote to me [al-Tabarani in M and A], saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, and he mentioned it with its chain like this, except that he said: "I buried eight daughters of mine in the Jahiliyyah." And at its end he said: "Then offer, if you wish, a camel for each one of them." Then he said:

My father narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from al-Aghar ibn al-Sabbah, from Khalifah ibn Husayn, who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I buried twelve daughters of mine in the Jahiliyyah, or thirteen." He said: "Free a number of souls equal to them." He said: "So he freed a number of souls equal to them. When the following year came, he brought a hundred she-camels and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is the charity of my people, in return for what I did to the Muslims.'" Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "We used to let them graze and called them al-Qaysiyyah." [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (18/338) through Yahya al-Hammani, from Qays ibn al-Rabi' similarly. Al-Hammani is weak, but he has a supporting narration here.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And when the pages are unfolded﴾. Al-Dahhak said: Each person is given his record in his right hand or his left. Qatadah said: "[Your record] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari (30/46), noted from the margin of the Shu'ab edition.]], O son of Adam, is dictated into it, then it is folded, then it is unfolded for you on the Day of Resurrection. So let a man look at what he has dictated into his record."

* *

His saying: ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾. Mujahid said: "Pulled off." Al-Suddi said: "Uncovered." Al-Dahhak said: "It is stripped away and departs."

* *

His saying: ﴿And when Hell is kindled﴾. Al-Suddi said: "It is heated." Qatadah said: "It is set ablaze." He said: "Only the wrath of Allah and the sins of the children of Adam kindle it."

* *

His saying: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾. Al-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: meaning, it is brought close to its people.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then a soul will know what it has presented﴾. This is the answer (al-jawab), meaning: when these matters occur, then every soul will know what it did, and that will be presented to it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that were a great distance﴾ [Al 'Imran: 30]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent ahead and what he left behind﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abdah narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Mutarrif informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: When the verse ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ was revealed, Umar said, when he reached ﴿Then a soul will know what it has presented﴾: "By this the narration has been set in motion."

**Commentary on Surah At-Takwir**

It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Bahir al-Qassas informed us that Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid al-San'ani informed him that he heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look at the Day of Resurrection as if he were seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, ﴿When the sky is split open﴾, and ﴿When the sky is torn apart﴾."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in this way, from Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Azim al-Anbari, from Abd al-Razzaq, with the same chain. [Footnote: Musnad (2/27); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3333. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ that it means: it became dark. Al-Awfi narrated from him that it means: it went away. Mujahid said: it perished and went away. Al-Dahhak said the same.

Qatadah said: its light went away. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿wrapped up﴾ means "ghawwarat" (it was made to set/sink).

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: ﴿wrapped up﴾ means: it was thrown away.

Abu Salih said: ﴿wrapped up﴾ means: it was cast down. He also reported from him: it was turned upside down. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it falls to the earth.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: The correct view in our opinion regarding this is that al-takwir (the wrapping) is the gathering of one thing onto another, from which comes the winding of a turban [which is wrapping it around the head], and like the rolling up (takwir) of garments, which is folding clothes one on top of another. So the meaning of His saying ﴿wrapped up﴾ is: its parts are gathered onto one another, then it is rolled up and thrown away, and when that is done to it, its light is extinguished. [Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (30/41). Note: in one manuscript, "على" appears instead of "إلى".]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and Amr ibn Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mujalid, from a shaykh of Bajilah, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: He said: Allah will wrap up the sun, the moon and the stars on the Day of Resurrection in the sea, and Allah will send a dabur wind (a west wind) which will set them ablaze with fire. Al-Sha'bi also said the same.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ibn Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding the words of Allah ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: "It is wrapped up in Hell." [Footnote: Also narrated by al-Daylami in his Musnad, as in al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti (8/426).]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Hayyan narrated to us, Durust ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Yazid al-Raqqashi narrated to us, Anas narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sun and the moon are two (thawran) crippled ones in the Fire." [Footnote: In the manuscripts, "nawran" appears, but the correct reading is with the letter thā' (thawran). Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/148). Ibn Hibban narrated it in al-Majruhin (1/293) through Durust ibn Ziyad with the same wording, and said regarding Durust ibn Ziyad: "He was very munkar in hadith; it is not permissible to argue with his report. He narrated from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, and then mentioned this hadith."]

This is a weak hadith, because Yazid al-Raqqashi is weak. What al-Bukhari narrated in the Sahih is without this addition. Then al-Bukhari said:

Musaddad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, Abd Allah al-Danaj narrated to us, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The sun and the moon will be wrapped up (yukawwaran) on the Day of Resurrection." [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3200.]

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, and this is his wording. He narrated it in the Book of "The Beginning of Creation." It would have been appropriate for him to mention it here or to repeat it, as is his habit in such cases! Al-Bazzar has narrated it and given a better transmission. He said:

Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Abd Allah al-Danaj, who said: I heard Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Qasri in this mosque, the Mosque of Kufah, and al-Hasan came and sat with him, and he narrated: Abu Hurayrah narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the sun and the moon are two lights in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Hasan said: "And what is their sin?" He said: "I narrate to you from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and you say: 'I suppose he said: And what is their sin?'"

Then al-Bazzar said: This is not narrated from Abu Hurayrah except through this chain, and Abd Allah al-Danaj did not narrate from Abu Salamah anything other than this hadith.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the stars fall (inkadarat)﴾, it means: they were scattered, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾ (Surah al-Infitar, 2). The original meaning of inkidar is to pour down (al-insiba).

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "There are six signs before the Day of Resurrection. While people are in their markets, the light of the sun goes away. While they are in that state, the stars are scattered. While they are in that state, the mountains fall upon the face of the earth, and they shake, tremble and become mixed up. The jinn flee to mankind and mankind flee to the jinn, and the beasts, birds and wild animals become mixed together, and they surge against one another." ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: he said: they were mixed together. ﴿And when the pregnant camels are neglected﴾: he said: their people abandon them. ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: he said: the jinn said: "We will bring you the news." He said: So they went to the sea, and behold, it was a fire blazing. He said: While they were in that state, the earth split open in one crack, down to the lowest seventh earth and up to the highest seventh heaven. He said: While they were in that state, the wind came upon them and killed them."

Ibn Jarir narrated it, and this is his wording, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated part of it. Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu Salih, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman and al-Dahhak said the same regarding ﴿And when the stars fall﴾: it means they were scattered.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾ means: they changed. Yazid ibn Abi Maryam narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding ﴿And when the stars fall﴾: he said: "They fall into Hell, and everyone who worshipped other than Allah is in Hell, except for what was of Jesus and his mother. If they had been content to be worshipped, they would have entered it." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with the previously mentioned chain.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, it means: they departed from their places and were blown away, so they left the earth level and bare.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the pregnant camels are neglected﴾: Ikrimah and Mujahid said: they are the pregnant she-camels. Mujahid said: ﴿neglected﴾ means left and let loose.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b and al-Dahhak said: their people abandoned them. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: they were not milked and their udders were not tied; their owners left them. Al-Dahhak said: they were left without a shepherd.

The meaning in all of this is close. The intended meaning is that the pregnant camels (ishar), which are the best of camels and the pregnant ones that have reached the tenth month of their pregnancy, whose singular is 'ushara', and which keep this name until they give birth, have been neglected by people, who are busy with other things, and with their care and benefit from them, although previously they had been the most desired of things to them, because of the great, terrifying and dreadful matter that overwhelms them, which is the matter of the Resurrection, the establishment of its causes, and the occurrence of its preliminaries.

It was said: Rather, this will happen on the Day of Resurrection, and its owners will see it in that state, with no way for them to reach it. It has also been said regarding the ishar that they are the clouds, which are held back from moving between heaven and earth because of the ruin of the world. It has also been said that they are the lands that are tithed (tu'ashsharu). It was said that they are the dwellings that were inhabited, which become abandoned because their people have gone. Imam Abu Abd Allah al-Qurtubi related all these opinions in his book "al-Tadhkirah," and he preferred that they are the camels, and attributed this to most people. [Footnote: Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah, pp. 212–213.]

I say: Rather, nothing is known from the earlier generations and the imams other than this. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾, it means: they are assembled, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies with its wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 38). Ibn Abbas said: every creature will be gathered, even the fly. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Suddi and others said the same. Qatadah also said regarding the explanation of this verse: these creatures will be [present], and Allah will decide concerning them what He wills.

Ikrimah said: their gathering is their death.

Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi narrated to me, Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, Husayn informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: He said: the gathering of the beasts is their death, and the gathering of everything is death, except the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym regarding ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: He said: the command of Allah came upon them. Sufyan said: my father said: I mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: their gathering is their death.

It has already been mentioned from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he said regarding ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: they became mixed together.

Ibn Jarir said: The more preferable view is that of the one who said ﴿gathered﴾ means "brought together," as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the birds gathered (mahshurah)﴾ (Surah Sad, 19), meaning: assembled.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze (sujjirat)﴾: Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to a man from the Jews: "Where is Hell?" He said: "The sea." He said: "I do not think he is except truthful." [Qur'an: ﴿And by the sea that is set ablaze (al-masjur)﴾ (Surah al-Tur, 6), ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ (sujjirat, with a lightened form).] [Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (30/43).]

Ibn Abbas and others said: Allah will send upon them the dabur wind, which will ignite them, and they will become fire blazing. The discussion of this has already been mentioned at His saying ﴿And by the sea that is set ablaze﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Tahir narrated to us, Abd al-Jabbar ibn Sulayman Abu Sulayman al-Naffat narrated to me (a righteous shaykh who resembles Malik ibn Anas), from Mu'awiyah ibn Sa'id, who said: This sea is a blessing (the Mediterranean, the Sea of the Romans) in the middle of the earth, and all the rivers pour into it, and the great sea pours into it, and at its bottom are wells sealed with copper. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will be set ablaze.

This is a strange and remarkable report. In Sunan Abi Dawud: "No one rides the sea except a pilgrim, a one performing umrah, or a warrior in the way of Allah, for beneath the sea is fire, and beneath the fire is sea," and the hadith... The discussion of it was previously mentioned in Surah Fatir. [Footnote: The discussion of the hadith did not previously occur in Surah Fatir. It is in Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2489, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with both of them.]

Mujahid and al-Hasan ibn Muslim said: ﴿sujjirat﴾ means "ignited (uqidat)." Al-Hasan said: it dried up. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: its water receded and went away, leaving not a drop in it. Al-Dahhak also said: ﴿sujjirat﴾ means "burst open (fujjirat)." Al-Suddi said: it was opened and made to flow. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: ﴿sujjirat﴾ means "overflowed."

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired (zuwwijat)﴾, it means: every kind is gathered with its counterpart, like His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 22).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "They are the peers (al-darba'), every man with every people whose deeds he used to do." That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And you will be three kinds: the companions of the right hand, what are the companions of the right hand; and the companions of the left hand, what are the companions of the left hand; and the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 7-10]. He said: They are the peers. [[Also narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/429).]]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through other chains, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that Umar addressed the people and recited ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾, and said: "Its pairing is that every group is joined to its own group." In another narration: "They are two men who do a deed by which they enter Paradise or the Fire." [[Also narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Hamdan, as cited in the author's Musnad Umar (2/620), through Khalaf ibn al-Walid, from Israel, from Simak, similarly. It was also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (2/284-285), from al-Thawri, from Simak, from al-Nu'man, and from Israel, from Simak, from al-Nu'man. And al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/515) through Sufyan, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

In another narration from al-Nu'man: Umar was asked about the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾, and he said: "A righteous man is paired with a righteous man, and an evil man is paired with an evil man in the Fire; that is the pairing of souls."

In another narration from al-Nu'man: Umar said to the people: "What do you say about the interpretation of this verse: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾?" They were silent. He said: "Rather, it is that a man is paired with his counterpart from the people of Paradise, and a man is paired with his counterpart from the people of the Fire." Then he recited: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "That is when people are in three kinds."

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "The likes among people are gathered together." Similarly said al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Hasan, and Qatadah. Ibn Jarir chose this view, and it is the correct one.

Another opinion regarding His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ash'ath [ibn Sawwar] [[Addition from M.]], from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "A valley flows from the base of the Throne with water between the two blasts, and the time between them is forty years. From it every creature that has decayed grows, whether human, bird, or beast. If a passer-by had known them before that, he would recognize them on the earth, having sprouted. Then the spirits are sent, and the bodies are paired with them." That is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾.

Similarly said Abu al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, and also al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: meaning, they are paired with bodies. It was also said: The believers are paired with the wide-eyed houris, and the disbelievers are paired with devils. This was related by al-Qurtubi in al-Tadhkirah. [[Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah (p. 213).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾. This is the reading of the majority: ﴿su'ilat﴾ [was asked]. The one buried alive (al-maw'udah) is the girl whom the people of the Jahiliyyah used to bury in the dust out of aversion to daughters. On the Day of Resurrection, the buried girl will be asked for what sin she was killed, so that this would be a threat to her killer. If the wronged one is asked, then what is the assumption about the wrongdoer?!

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked﴾, meaning: she demanded. Similarly said Abu al-Duha: "She demanded," meaning: she sought retribution for her blood. And from al-Suddi and Qatadah, the same. [[See Tafsir al-Tabari (30/45) and al-Bahr al-Muhit of Abu Hayyan (8/433).]]

Traditions have been related concerning the buried girl. Imam Ahmad said:
Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Abu al-Aswad, namely Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal, narrated to me, from Urwah, from Aishah, from Judamah bint Wahb, the sister of Ukkashah, who said: I attended the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among some people, and he was saying: "I had intended to forbid ghilah (secret intercourse during breastfeeding), but I looked at the Romans and the Persians, and they practice ghilah with their children, and that does not harm their children at all." Then they asked him about 'azl (coitus interruptus), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is the hidden burial (al-wad' al-khafi), and it is the one of whom it is said: ﴿the buried girl will be asked﴾."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri', namely Abd Allah ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub. [[Al-Musnad (6/434) and Sahih Muslim, no. 1442.]] Ibn Majah also narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yahya ibn Ishaq al-Sayhalini, from Yahya ibn Ayyub. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2011.]] Muslim also narrated it, as did Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Malik ibn Anas; all three from Abu al-Aswad, with the same chain. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1442; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3882; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2077; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/106).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Alqamah, from Salamah ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, who said: My brother and I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, our mother Mulaykah used to keep the ties of kinship, host guests, and do [and do] [[Addition from M or al-Musnad.]], and she died in the Jahiliyyah. Will that benefit her at all?" He said: "No." We said: "She used to bury our sister alive in the Jahiliyyah. Will that benefit her at all?" He said: "The one who buries and the one who is buried are in the Fire, unless Islam reaches the one who buries, and Allah pardons her."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (3/478) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11649.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Alqamah and Abu al-Ahwas, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one who buries and the one who is buried are in the Fire." [[Also narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4717, through Abu Ishaq, from Amir, from Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud. It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/114), through Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi, from Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud.]]

Ahmad also said: Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, Awf informed us, Hasna' bint Mu'awiyah al-Suraymiyyah narrated to me, from her paternal uncle, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is in Paradise?" He said: "The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyr is in Paradise, the newborn is in Paradise, and the buried girl is in Paradise." [[Al-Musnad (5/58).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Qurrah narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is in Paradise?" He said: "The buried girl is in Paradise."

This is a mursal hadith from the mursal narrations of al-Hasan, and some have accepted it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Zahrani narrated to me, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The children of the polytheists are in Paradise. Whoever claims that they are in the Fire has lied. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾." Ibn Abbas said: "She is the one buried."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel informed us, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked [for what sin she was killed]﴾ [[Addition from A.]], who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I buried daughters of mine alive in the Jahiliyyah." He said: "Free a slave for each one of them." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a man with camels?" He said: "Then sacrifice a camel for each one of them."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar, the hafiz, said: Abd al-Razzaq was contradicted in this, and we did not write it except from al-Husayn ibn Mahdi, from him. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2280 (Kashf al-Astar).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, saying: Abu Abd Allah al-Zahrani informed us, in what he wrote to me [al-Tabarani in M and A], saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, and he mentioned it with its chain like this, except that he said: "I buried eight daughters of mine in the Jahiliyyah." And at its end he said: "Then offer, if you wish, a camel for each one of them." Then he said:

My father narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from al-Aghar ibn al-Sabbah, from Khalifah ibn Husayn, who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I buried twelve daughters of mine in the Jahiliyyah, or thirteen." He said: "Free a number of souls equal to them." He said: "So he freed a number of souls equal to them. When the following year came, he brought a hundred she-camels and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is the charity of my people, in return for what I did to the Muslims.'" Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "We used to let them graze and called them al-Qaysiyyah." [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (18/338) through Yahya al-Hammani, from Qays ibn al-Rabi' similarly. Al-Hammani is weak, but he has a supporting narration here.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And when the pages are unfolded﴾. Al-Dahhak said: Each person is given his record in his right hand or his left. Qatadah said: "[Your record] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari (30/46), noted from the margin of the Shu'ab edition.]], O son of Adam, is dictated into it, then it is folded, then it is unfolded for you on the Day of Resurrection. So let a man look at what he has dictated into his record."

* *

His saying: ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾. Mujahid said: "Pulled off." Al-Suddi said: "Uncovered." Al-Dahhak said: "It is stripped away and departs."

* *

His saying: ﴿And when Hell is kindled﴾. Al-Suddi said: "It is heated." Qatadah said: "It is set ablaze." He said: "Only the wrath of Allah and the sins of the children of Adam kindle it."

* *

His saying: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾. Al-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: meaning, it is brought close to its people.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then a soul will know what it has presented﴾. This is the answer (al-jawab), meaning: when these matters occur, then every soul will know what it did, and that will be presented to it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that were a great distance﴾ [Al 'Imran: 30]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent ahead and what he left behind﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abdah narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Mutarrif informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: When the verse ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ was revealed, Umar said, when he reached ﴿Then a soul will know what it has presented﴾: "By this the narration has been set in motion."

**Commentary on Surah At-Takwir**

It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Bahir al-Qassas informed us that Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid al-San'ani informed him that he heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look at the Day of Resurrection as if he were seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, ﴿When the sky is split open﴾, and ﴿When the sky is torn apart﴾."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in this way, from Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Azim al-Anbari, from Abd al-Razzaq, with the same chain. [Footnote: Musnad (2/27); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3333. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ that it means: it became dark. Al-Awfi narrated from him that it means: it went away. Mujahid said: it perished and went away. Al-Dahhak said the same.

Qatadah said: its light went away. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿wrapped up﴾ means "ghawwarat" (it was made to set/sink).

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: ﴿wrapped up﴾ means: it was thrown away.

Abu Salih said: ﴿wrapped up﴾ means: it was cast down. He also reported from him: it was turned upside down. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it falls to the earth.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: The correct view in our opinion regarding this is that al-takwir (the wrapping) is the gathering of one thing onto another, from which comes the winding of a turban [which is wrapping it around the head], and like the rolling up (takwir) of garments, which is folding clothes one on top of another. So the meaning of His saying ﴿wrapped up﴾ is: its parts are gathered onto one another, then it is rolled up and thrown away, and when that is done to it, its light is extinguished. [Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (30/41). Note: in one manuscript, "على" appears instead of "إلى".]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and Amr ibn Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mujalid, from a shaykh of Bajilah, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: He said: Allah will wrap up the sun, the moon and the stars on the Day of Resurrection in the sea, and Allah will send a dabur wind (a west wind) which will set them ablaze with fire. Al-Sha'bi also said the same.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ibn Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding the words of Allah ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: "It is wrapped up in Hell." [Footnote: Also narrated by al-Daylami in his Musnad, as in al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti (8/426).]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Hayyan narrated to us, Durust ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Yazid al-Raqqashi narrated to us, Anas narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sun and the moon are two (thawran) crippled ones in the Fire." [Footnote: In the manuscripts, "nawran" appears, but the correct reading is with the letter thā' (thawran). Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/148). Ibn Hibban narrated it in al-Majruhin (1/293) through Durust ibn Ziyad with the same wording, and said regarding Durust ibn Ziyad: "He was very munkar in hadith; it is not permissible to argue with his report. He narrated from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, and then mentioned this hadith."]

This is a weak hadith, because Yazid al-Raqqashi is weak. What al-Bukhari narrated in the Sahih is without this addition. Then al-Bukhari said:

Musaddad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, Abd Allah al-Danaj narrated to us, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The sun and the moon will be wrapped up (yukawwaran) on the Day of Resurrection." [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3200.]

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, and this is his wording. He narrated it in the Book of "The Beginning of Creation." It would have been appropriate for him to mention it here or to repeat it, as is his habit in such cases! Al-Bazzar has narrated it and given a better transmission. He said:

Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Abd Allah al-Danaj, who said: I heard Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Qasri in this mosque, the Mosque of Kufah, and al-Hasan came and sat with him, and he narrated: Abu Hurayrah narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the sun and the moon are two lights in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Hasan said: "And what is their sin?" He said: "I narrate to you from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and you say: 'I suppose he said: And what is their sin?'"

Then al-Bazzar said: This is not narrated from Abu Hurayrah except through this chain, and Abd Allah al-Danaj did not narrate from Abu Salamah anything other than this hadith.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the stars fall (inkadarat)﴾, it means: they were scattered, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾ (Surah al-Infitar, 2). The original meaning of inkidar is to pour down (al-insiba).

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "There are six signs before the Day of Resurrection. While people are in their markets, the light of the sun goes away. While they are in that state, the stars are scattered. While they are in that state, the mountains fall upon the face of the earth, and they shake, tremble and become mixed up. The jinn flee to mankind and mankind flee to the jinn, and the beasts, birds and wild animals become mixed together, and they surge against one another." ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: he said: they were mixed together. ﴿And when the pregnant camels are neglected﴾: he said: their people abandon them. ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: he said: the jinn said: "We will bring you the news." He said: So they went to the sea, and behold, it was a fire blazing. He said: While they were in that state, the earth split open in one crack, down to the lowest seventh earth and up to the highest seventh heaven. He said: While they were in that state, the wind came upon them and killed them."

Ibn Jarir narrated it, and this is his wording, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated part of it. Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu Salih, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman and al-Dahhak said the same regarding ﴿And when the stars fall﴾: it means they were scattered.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾ means: they changed. Yazid ibn Abi Maryam narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding ﴿And when the stars fall﴾: he said: "They fall into Hell, and everyone who worshipped other than Allah is in Hell, except for what was of Jesus and his mother. If they had been content to be worshipped, they would have entered it." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with the previously mentioned chain.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, it means: they departed from their places and were blown away, so they left the earth level and bare.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the pregnant camels are neglected﴾: Ikrimah and Mujahid said: they are the pregnant she-camels. Mujahid said: ﴿neglected﴾ means left and let loose.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b and al-Dahhak said: their people abandoned them. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: they were not milked and their udders were not tied; their owners left them. Al-Dahhak said: they were left without a shepherd.

The meaning in all of this is close. The intended meaning is that the pregnant camels (ishar), which are the best of camels and the pregnant ones that have reached the tenth month of their pregnancy, whose singular is 'ushara', and which keep this name until they give birth, have been neglected by people, who are busy with other things, and with their care and benefit from them, although previously they had been the most desired of things to them, because of the great, terrifying and dreadful matter that overwhelms them, which is the matter of the Resurrection, the establishment of its causes, and the occurrence of its preliminaries.

It was said: Rather, this will happen on the Day of Resurrection, and its owners will see it in that state, with no way for them to reach it. It has also been said regarding the ishar that they are the clouds, which are held back from moving between heaven and earth because of the ruin of the world. It has also been said that they are the lands that are tithed (tu'ashsharu). It was said that they are the dwellings that were inhabited, which become abandoned because their people have gone. Imam Abu Abd Allah al-Qurtubi related all these opinions in his book "al-Tadhkirah," and he preferred that they are the camels, and attributed this to most people. [Footnote: Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah, pp. 212–213.]

I say: Rather, nothing is known from the earlier generations and the imams other than this. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾, it means: they are assembled, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies with its wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 38). Ibn Abbas said: every creature will be gathered, even the fly. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Suddi and others said the same. Qatadah also said regarding the explanation of this verse: these creatures will be [present], and Allah will decide concerning them what He wills.

Ikrimah said: their gathering is their death.

Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi narrated to me, Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, Husayn informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: He said: the gathering of the beasts is their death, and the gathering of everything is death, except the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym regarding ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: He said: the command of Allah came upon them. Sufyan said: my father said: I mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: their gathering is their death.

It has already been mentioned from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he said regarding ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: they became mixed together.

Ibn Jarir said: The more preferable view is that of the one who said ﴿gathered﴾ means "brought together," as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the birds gathered (mahshurah)﴾ (Surah Sad, 19), meaning: assembled.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze (sujjirat)﴾: Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to us, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to a man from the Jews: "Where is Hell?" He said: "The sea." He said: "I do not think he is except truthful." [Qur'an: ﴿And by the sea that is set ablaze (al-masjur)﴾ (Surah al-Tur, 6), ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ (sujjirat, with a lightened form).] [Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (30/43).]

Ibn Abbas and others said: Allah will send upon them the dabur wind, which will ignite them, and they will become fire blazing. The discussion of this has already been mentioned at His saying ﴿And by the sea that is set ablaze﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Abu Tahir narrated to us, Abd al-Jabbar ibn Sulayman Abu Sulayman al-Naffat narrated to me (a righteous shaykh who resembles Malik ibn Anas), from Mu'awiyah ibn Sa'id, who said: This sea is a blessing (the Mediterranean, the Sea of the Romans) in the middle of the earth, and all the rivers pour into it, and the great sea pours into it, and at its bottom are wells sealed with copper. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will be set ablaze.

This is a strange and remarkable report. In Sunan Abi Dawud: "No one rides the sea except a pilgrim, a one performing umrah, or a warrior in the way of Allah, for beneath the sea is fire, and beneath the fire is sea," and the hadith... The discussion of it was previously mentioned in Surah Fatir. [Footnote: The discussion of the hadith did not previously occur in Surah Fatir. It is in Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2489, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with both of them.]

Mujahid and al-Hasan ibn Muslim said: ﴿sujjirat﴾ means "ignited (uqidat)." Al-Hasan said: it dried up. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: its water receded and went away, leaving not a drop in it. Al-Dahhak also said: ﴿sujjirat﴾ means "burst open (fujjirat)." Al-Suddi said: it was opened and made to flow. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: ﴿sujjirat﴾ means "overflowed."

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired (zuwwijat)﴾, it means: every kind is gathered with its counterpart, like His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 22).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "They are the peers (al-darba'), every man with every people whose deeds he used to do." That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And you will be three kinds: the companions of the right hand, what are the companions of the right hand; and the companions of the left hand, what are the companions of the left hand; and the foremost, the foremost﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 7-10]. He said: They are the peers. [[Also narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/429).]]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through other chains, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that Umar addressed the people and recited ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾, and said: "Its pairing is that every group is joined to its own group." In another narration: "They are two men who do a deed by which they enter Paradise or the Fire." [[Also narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Hamdan, as cited in the author's Musnad Umar (2/620), through Khalaf ibn al-Walid, from Israel, from Simak, similarly. It was also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (2/284-285), from al-Thawri, from Simak, from al-Nu'man, and from Israel, from Simak, from al-Nu'man. And al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/515) through Sufyan, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

In another narration from al-Nu'man: Umar was asked about the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾, and he said: "A righteous man is paired with a righteous man, and an evil man is paired with an evil man in the Fire; that is the pairing of souls."

In another narration from al-Nu'man: Umar said to the people: "What do you say about the interpretation of this verse: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾?" They were silent. He said: "Rather, it is that a man is paired with his counterpart from the people of Paradise, and a man is paired with his counterpart from the people of the Fire." Then he recited: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "That is when people are in three kinds."

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "The likes among people are gathered together." Similarly said al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Hasan, and Qatadah. Ibn Jarir chose this view, and it is the correct one.

Another opinion regarding His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ash'ath [ibn Sawwar] [[Addition from M.]], from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "A valley flows from the base of the Throne with water between the two blasts, and the time between them is forty years. From it every creature that has decayed grows, whether human, bird, or beast. If a passer-by had known them before that, he would recognize them on the earth, having sprouted. Then the spirits are sent, and the bodies are paired with them." That is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾.

Similarly said Abu al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, and also al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His saying ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: meaning, they are paired with bodies. It was also said: The believers are paired with the wide-eyed houris, and the disbelievers are paired with devils. This was related by al-Qurtubi in al-Tadhkirah. [[Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah (p. 213).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾. This is the reading of the majority: ﴿su'ilat﴾ [was asked]. The one buried alive (al-maw'udah) is the girl whom the people of the Jahiliyyah used to bury in the dust out of aversion to daughters. On the Day of Resurrection, the buried girl will be asked for what sin she was killed, so that this would be a threat to her killer. If the wronged one is asked, then what is the assumption about the wrongdoer?!

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked﴾, meaning: she demanded. Similarly said Abu al-Duha: "She demanded," meaning: she sought retribution for her blood. And from al-Suddi and Qatadah, the same. [[See Tafsir al-Tabari (30/45) and al-Bahr al-Muhit of Abu Hayyan (8/433).]]

Traditions have been related concerning the buried girl. Imam Ahmad said:
Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Abu al-Aswad, namely Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal, narrated to me, from Urwah, from Aishah, from Judamah bint Wahb, the sister of Ukkashah, who said: I attended the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among some people, and he was saying: "I had intended to forbid ghilah (secret intercourse during breastfeeding), but I looked at the Romans and the Persians, and they practice ghilah with their children, and that does not harm their children at all." Then they asked him about 'azl (coitus interruptus), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is the hidden burial (al-wad' al-khafi), and it is the one of whom it is said: ﴿the buried girl will be asked﴾."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri', namely Abd Allah ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub. [[Al-Musnad (6/434) and Sahih Muslim, no. 1442.]] Ibn Majah also narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yahya ibn Ishaq al-Sayhalini, from Yahya ibn Ayyub. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2011.]] Muslim also narrated it, as did Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Malik ibn Anas; all three from Abu al-Aswad, with the same chain. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 1442; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 3882; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2077; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/106).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Alqamah, from Salamah ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, who said: My brother and I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, our mother Mulaykah used to keep the ties of kinship, host guests, and do [and do] [[Addition from M or al-Musnad.]], and she died in the Jahiliyyah. Will that benefit her at all?" He said: "No." We said: "She used to bury our sister alive in the Jahiliyyah. Will that benefit her at all?" He said: "The one who buries and the one who is buried are in the Fire, unless Islam reaches the one who buries, and Allah pardons her."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (3/478) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11649.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Alqamah and Abu al-Ahwas, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The one who buries and the one who is buried are in the Fire." [[Also narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4717, through Abu Ishaq, from Amir, from Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud. It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/114), through Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi, from Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud.]]

Ahmad also said: Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, Awf informed us, Hasna' bint Mu'awiyah al-Suraymiyyah narrated to me, from her paternal uncle, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is in Paradise?" He said: "The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyr is in Paradise, the newborn is in Paradise, and the buried girl is in Paradise." [[Al-Musnad (5/58).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Qurrah narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is in Paradise?" He said: "The buried girl is in Paradise."

This is a mursal hadith from the mursal narrations of al-Hasan, and some have accepted it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Zahrani narrated to me, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The children of the polytheists are in Paradise. Whoever claims that they are in the Fire has lied. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked, for what sin she was killed﴾." Ibn Abbas said: "She is the one buried."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Israel informed us, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked [for what sin she was killed]﴾ [[Addition from A.]], who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I buried daughters of mine alive in the Jahiliyyah." He said: "Free a slave for each one of them." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a man with camels?" He said: "Then sacrifice a camel for each one of them."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar, the hafiz, said: Abd al-Razzaq was contradicted in this, and we did not write it except from al-Husayn ibn Mahdi, from him. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2280 (Kashf al-Astar).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, saying: Abu Abd Allah al-Zahrani informed us, in what he wrote to me [al-Tabarani in M and A], saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, and he mentioned it with its chain like this, except that he said: "I buried eight daughters of mine in the Jahiliyyah." And at its end he said: "Then offer, if you wish, a camel for each one of them." Then he said:

My father narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from al-Aghar ibn al-Sabbah, from Khalifah ibn Husayn, who said: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I buried twelve daughters of mine in the Jahiliyyah, or thirteen." He said: "Free a number of souls equal to them." He said: "So he freed a number of souls equal to them. When the following year came, he brought a hundred she-camels and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is the charity of my people, in return for what I did to the Muslims.'" Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "We used to let them graze and called them al-Qaysiyyah." [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (18/338) through Yahya al-Hammani, from Qays ibn al-Rabi' similarly. Al-Hammani is weak, but he has a supporting narration here.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And when the pages are unfolded﴾. Al-Dahhak said: Each person is given his record in his right hand or his left. Qatadah said: "[Your record] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari (30/46), noted from the margin of the Shu'ab edition.]], O son of Adam, is dictated into it, then it is folded, then it is unfolded for you on the Day of Resurrection. So let a man look at what he has dictated into his record."

* *

His saying: ﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾. Mujahid said: "Pulled off." Al-Suddi said: "Uncovered." Al-Dahhak said: "It is stripped away and departs."

* *

His saying: ﴿And when Hell is kindled﴾. Al-Suddi said: "It is heated." Qatadah said: "It is set ablaze." He said: "Only the wrath of Allah and the sins of the children of Adam kindle it."

* *

His saying: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾. Al-Dahhak, Abu Malik, Qatadah, and al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: meaning, it is brought close to its people.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then a soul will know what it has presented﴾. This is the answer (al-jawab), meaning: when these matters occur, then every soul will know what it did, and that will be presented to it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that were a great distance﴾ [Al 'Imran: 30]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent ahead and what he left behind﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abdah narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Mutarrif informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: When the verse ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ was revealed, Umar said, when he reached ﴿Then a soul will know what it has presented﴾: "By this the narration has been set in motion."

**Commentary on Surah At-Takwir**

It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Bahir al-Qassas informed us that Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid al-San'ani informed him that he heard Ibn Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would like to look at the Day of Resurrection as if he were seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, ﴿When the sky is split open﴾, and ﴿When the sky is torn apart﴾."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in this way, from Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Azim al-Anbari, from Abd al-Razzaq, with the same chain. [Footnote: Musnad (2/27); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3333. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ that it means: it became dark. Al-Awfi narrated from him that it means: it went away. Mujahid said: it perished and went away. Al-Dahhak said the same.

Qatadah said: its light went away. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿wrapped up﴾ means "ghawwarat" (it was made to set/sink).

Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: ﴿wrapped up﴾ means: it was thrown away.

Abu Salih said: ﴿wrapped up﴾ means: it was cast down. He also reported from him: it was turned upside down. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it falls to the earth.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: The correct view in our opinion regarding this is that al-takwir (the wrapping) is the gathering of one thing onto another, from which comes the winding of a turban [which is wrapping it around the head], and like the rolling up (takwir) of garments, which is folding clothes one on top of another. So the meaning of His saying ﴿wrapped up﴾ is: its parts are gathered onto one another, then it is rolled up and thrown away, and when that is done to it, its light is extinguished. [Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (30/41). Note: in one manuscript, "على" appears instead of "إلى".]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and Amr ibn Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mujalid, from a shaykh of Bajilah, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: He said: Allah will wrap up the sun, the moon and the stars on the Day of Resurrection in the sea, and Allah will send a dabur wind (a west wind) which will set them ablaze with fire. Al-Sha'bi also said the same.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ibn Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding the words of Allah ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: "It is wrapped up in Hell." [Footnote: Also narrated by al-Daylami in his Musnad, as in al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti (8/426).]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Hayyan narrated to us, Durust ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Yazid al-Raqqashi narrated to us, Anas narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sun and the moon are two (thawran) crippled ones in the Fire." [Footnote: In the manuscripts, "nawran" appears, but the correct reading is with the letter thā' (thawran). Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/148). Ibn Hibban narrated it in al-Majruhin (1/293) through Durust ibn Ziyad with the same wording, and said regarding Durust ibn Ziyad: "He was very munkar in hadith; it is not permissible to argue with his report. He narrated from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, and then mentioned this hadith."]

This is a weak hadith, because Yazid al-Raqqashi is weak. What al-Bukhari narrated in the Sahih is without this addition. Then al-Bukhari said:

Musaddad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, Abd Allah al-Danaj narrated to us, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The sun and the moon will be wrapped up (yukawwaran) on the Day of Resurrection." [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3200.]

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, and this is his wording. He narrated it in the Book of "The Beginning of Creation." It would have been appropriate for him to mention it here or to repeat it, as is his habit in such cases! Al-Bazzar has narrated it and given a better transmission. He said:

Ibrahim ibn Ziyad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Abd Allah al-Danaj, who said: I heard Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah al-Qasri in this mosque, the Mosque of Kufah, and al-Hasan came and sat with him, and he narrated: Abu Hurayrah narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the sun and the moon are two lights in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Hasan said: "And what is their sin?" He said: "I narrate to you from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and you say: 'I suppose he said: And what is their sin?'"

Then al-Bazzar said: This is not narrated from Abu Hurayrah except through this chain, and Abd Allah al-Danaj did not narrate from Abu Salamah anything other than this hadith.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the stars fall (inkadarat)﴾, it means: they were scattered, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾ (Surah al-Infitar, 2). The original meaning of inkidar is to pour down (al-insiba).

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "There are six signs before the Day of Resurrection. While people are in their markets, the light of the sun goes away. While they are in that state, the stars are scattered. While they are in that state, the mountains fall upon the face of the earth, and they shake, tremble and become mixed up. The jinn flee to mankind and mankind flee to the jinn, and the beasts, birds and wild animals become mixed together, and they surge against one another." ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: he said: they were mixed together. ﴿And when the pregnant camels are neglected﴾: he said: their people abandon them. ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: he said: the jinn said: "We will bring you the news." He said: So they went to the sea, and behold, it was a fire blazing. He said: While they were in that state, the earth split open in one crack, down to the lowest seventh earth and up to the highest seventh heaven. He said: While they were in that state, the wind came upon them and killed them."

Ibn Jarir narrated it, and this is his wording, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated part of it. Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, al-Hasan al-Basri, Abu Salih, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman and al-Dahhak said the same regarding ﴿And when the stars fall﴾: it means they were scattered.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾ means: they changed. Yazid ibn Abi Maryam narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding ﴿And when the stars fall﴾: he said: "They fall into Hell, and everyone who worshipped other than Allah is in Hell, except for what was of Jesus and his mother. If they had been content to be worshipped, they would have entered it." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with the previously mentioned chain.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, it means: they departed from their places and were blown away, so they left the earth level and bare.

* *
